claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts are highly atomically disordered solid solutions.
The highly disordered atomic arrangement creates an ensemble of active surface sites.
The active-site ensemble produced by atomic disorder mitigates poisoning by ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Mitigation of intermediate poisoning allows the disordered catalyst to maintain durability.
Annealing at approximately 200°C for one hour in an inert atmosphere will induce partial atomic ordering.
The proposed mild annealing treatment can induce ordering without significant particle sintering.
Increasing atomic order will disrupt the surface distribution of active catalytic ensembles.
Atomic disorder produces a wider distribution of adsorption energies.
The wider adsorption-energy distribution favors moderate binding of ethanol and its intermediates.
Moderate binding limits strong poisoning and thereby improves durability.
Increasing atomic order narrows the adsorption-energy distribution.
More ordered ensembles can bind intermediates such as CO or acetaldehyde species too strongly.
Stronger binding of poisoning intermediates accelerates catalyst deactivation.
Relative to the untreated disordered baseline, the annealed catalyst will exhibit a faster decline in catalytic current or activity during ethanol oxidation.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs baseline has demonstrated strong initial ethanol-oxidation performance and durability.
The proposed ordering–durability relationship is expected to hold for approximately 5–10 nm particles in acidic electrolyte near 60°C when annealing does not cause significant sintering.
